subject.title: Per-agent compaction and contextPruning overrides in agents.list

question: Should OpenClaw adopt per-agent `compaction` and `contextPruning` overrides as a supported `agents.list[]` config surface, and should the active open PR be repaired, narrowed, or declined?
rationale: The request is a valid core-runtime capability gap, but it adds new strict config/default behavior with session-state and provider-routing consequences that automation should not permanently define without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt Through Active PR
options.body: Approve the additive per-agent config surface and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 as the landing or repair path after proof and review gaps are resolved.

options.title: Narrow To Compaction Model First
options.body: Accept only `agents.list[].compaction.model` initially and defer broader compaction/contextPruning merge semantics until maintainers choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Defer The Config Surface
options.body: Decline this config expansion for now and keep users on global defaults or separate instances until a smaller product direction is agreed.

recommendation.title: Adopt Through Active PR
recommendation.body: Approve the additive per-agent config surface and use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88506 as the landing or repair path after proof and review gaps are resolved.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is config-surface/product-direction heavy, and this account has recent adjacent history on agent runtime and config normalization plus prior triage comments in this cluster.
